Change numbers are unique across `.sdd/` and `.sdd/_archive/` and are never reused.
Unknown entries in `.sdd/` are preserved byte-identical by every command.
The registry equals the rebuild from frontmatter, apart from `generated_at`; any difference is drift (`LINT-REG-001`).
No change may enter ideation unless the constitution is approved (G0).
`profile` may change only from lite to full.
A stopped or archived change accepts no phase start, gate or task update.
`implementation.status` is a function of the task statuses (state-machines §5).
A phase is `approved` only if its recomputed hash equals `approved_hash`; otherwise it is `stale`.
A phase can be started only when its predecessor is `approved` (G1 → spec, G2 → plan).
When a phase leaves `approved`, every later approved phase of the change becomes `stale`.
Generated artifacts are excluded from phase hashes and are never hand-edited (overwritten by the next generation).
An ID is defined at most once in the workspace (TR-13).
Every referenced ID is defined or tombstoned (TR-12).
An AcceptanceCriterion belongs to exactly one Requirement, whose sequence number appears in the AC ID.
The traceability rules TR-01 … TR-15 of C001-IF-04 §5 hold for an approved phase, except for items waived at its gate.
No allocated or tombstoned ID is ever allocated again (C001-REQ-110).
`ref` is an ID defined in the change when the defect is created.
A change with an open defect cannot be archived.
A waiver exists only as part of a successful approval; waivers are never removed, only superseded by a later gate record.
Every phase status change to `approved` has exactly one GateRecord with decision approve or approve-with-waivers and a non-empty note.
An `inventory_only: true` file contains no requirement entry.
Every requirement in `_living/` came from an archived change whose G3 was approved.
Rounds contain 1–4 questions; options per question 2–3 with the recommended one first.
An evidence entry with layer `grep` has confidence at most `medium` (no semantic resolution).
